name: review the plan before it goes for approval
about: A fresh agent reads the whole plan and tells the planner what is wrong with it, before Andrew is asked anything. OPTIONAL, and it is the one library step nothing brings with it: no definition composes it and no definition obliges it, so it is in a plan because the planner decided the planning risk earned it. Name it when the approach has meaningful tradeoffs, when the plan crosses subsystems, when several agents or handoffs are proposed, when verification is expensive or incomplete, or when failure would have a large blast radius. A small linear plan does not get one and goes straight to Andrew — a reviewer added to bounded work with an obvious approach is the process this design exists to remove. WHAT THE REVIEWER CHECKS: that every success criterion is covered by a step, that the deps and handoffs are coherent, that work which did not need separating was left with one agent, that every model, tool, skill, preset and capability named really exists — checked against `sb plugin plans catalog`, which is generated from this repo — and that the budgets, the termination condition and the verification match the risk. Exact names are checked; qualitative advice is left alone. IT IS READ-ONLY ON THE PLAN, and that is the whole boundary: the reviewer reports its findings to the planner with `sb tell`, and never edits the plan file, never reshapes the plan, never approves it and never ticks this step. Shape stays with the planner and approval stays with Andrew. THE PLANNER RESOLVES THE FINDINGS, then puts a COMPACT result in this step's `output` — the findings and what was done about each, a line apiece — and only then ticks it. Compact because the plan is beside it and a second copy of the plan is once too many. WIRING IT, which is yours to do by hand: this step and `change-approval` share the `design` band, and an anchor only places a step after a band BELOW it, so both are minted as marked starts with no edge between them. Put this step's id in the approval step's `deps` and set that step's `root` to false, in the plan file, in the same edit — a start mark and a dep on one step say opposite things and `validate` reports the pair. Without that edit the plan reads as one where the approval can be reached without the review. ON A REJECTION at the approval, the work comes back to the SAME planner: it redoes the design, bumps that step's `tries`, puts it back to `open` and blocks again. This review is repeated only where the revised planning risk earns it a second time; a wording change to a contract Andrew rejected does not.
